claims.text: Streaming connectors do not run get_identities().
claims.excerpt: their indexing implementations do not run the optional get_identities() crawl.

claims.text: Unknown groups match nobody.
claims.excerpt: An ACL naming a group Glean has never heard of matches nobody.

claims.text: A connector is a data client plus a connector class.
claims.excerpt: A connector is two classes: a data client that fetches records from your source, and a connector that turns them into Glean documents.

claims.text: The SDK owns batching, retries, upload sessions, and stale-document cleanup.
claims.excerpt: SDK owns batching, retries, upload sessions, and stale-document cleanup.

claims.text: The SDK is a client for the Indexing API.
claims.excerpt: The SDK is a client for the Indexing API, not a replacement - the API documentation stays the reference for the wire protocol.

claims.text: SDK config: two env vars.
claims.excerpt: Two environment variables. There is no configuration file.

claims.text: GLEAN_SERVER_URL is the Glean backend URL.
claims.excerpt: GLEAN_SERVER_URLYour Glean backend URL

claims.text: GLEAN_INDEXING_API_TOKEN is a datasource-scoped Indexing API token.
claims.excerpt: GLEAN_INDEXING_API_TOKENDatasource-scoped Indexing API token.

claims.text: Missing env vars fail at construction.
claims.excerpt: A missing variable raises MissingEnvironmentVariableError at client construction, not mid-upload.

claims.text: SDK errors derive from GleanError.
claims.excerpt: Every SDK exception derives from GleanError and carries a fix_suggestion

claims.text: In the SDK identity crawl, users are bulk-indexed first; groups without memberships raise InconsistentDataError.
claims.excerpt: Users are bulk-indexed first. If groups are returned, memberships must be too - otherwise the SDK raises InconsistentDataError, because groups without memberships produce ACLs that can never match anyone.

claims.text: On an incremental crawl the SDK calls _get_last_crawl_timestamp(); the base implementation returns None.
claims.excerpt: On an incremental crawl, calls _get_last_crawl_timestamp(). The base implementation returns None.

claims.text: Full = replacement; incremental = additive.
claims.excerpt: A full crawl calls PushUploader.bulk_index_documents() for replacement and stale cleanup. An incremental crawl calls additive index_documents().

claims.text: Failures exit non-zero.
claims.excerpt: On exception, increments the error counter and re-raises so a scheduler sees a non-zero exit.

claims.text: Use the streaming connector when the dataset is large or paginated and the source client is synchronous.
claims.excerpt: The dataset is large or paginated and your source client is synchronous.

claims.text: The async streaming connector uses async generators and is driven with index_data_async().
claims.excerpt: Same model, async generators. Drive it with index_data_async().

claims.text: Employee data is separate from ACL identities.
claims.excerpt: It's distinct from the datasource identities (users, groups, memberships) that back document ACLs

claims.text: Start with BaseDatasourceConnector if unsure; switching to streaming changes the base class and get_source_data() return type, not transform().
claims.excerpt: If you're unsure, start with BaseDatasourceConnector. Switching to a streaming variant later means changing the base class and the return type of get_source_data() - transform() is unchanged.

claims.text: Memory limits need streaming, not smaller batches.
claims.excerpt: the fix is a streaming connector, not a smaller batch size, because batching happens after transform.

claims.text: batch_size defaults to 1000.
claims.excerpt: All four classes expose batch_size, defaulting to 1000.

claims.text: The SDK HTTP client retries 429, 500, 502, 503, 504; everything else fails immediately.
claims.excerpt: retry_status_codes{429, 500, 502, 503, 504}Everything else fails immediately.

claims.text: Default retries: one retry.
claims.excerpt: The default max_attempts=2 is deliberately conservative - one retry.

claims.text: Production connectors should raise max_attempts to 4 or 5 against aggressive rate limiters.
claims.excerpt: production connectors should raise it to 4 or 5, particularly against APIs that rate-limit aggressively.

claims.text: Rate limiting is proactive; retries are reactive.
claims.excerpt: The rate limiter is proactive

claims.text: Run below the source quota.
claims.excerpt: A source allowing 600 requests/minute is 10/second; running at 7-8 leaves room for retries

claims.text: SDK cursor paging stops when the cursor is missing, empty, not a string, or repeated.
claims.excerpt: Paging stops when the cursor is missing, empty, not a string, or identical to the previous cursor.

claims.text: Offset pagination is unstable under writes.
claims.excerpt: Offset pagination is unstable against a source being written to during the crawl.

claims.text: Paging loops must terminate.
claims.excerpt: Whatever loop you write must terminate on a source that misbehaves.

claims.text: Query params are redacted in logs.
claims.excerpt: PullOptions.mask_params defaults to True, so query parameters are redacted in the client's request logs.

claims.text: Redaction covers logs only.
claims.excerpt: Redaction covers logging only.

claims.text: Full crawls must cover the entire scope.
claims.excerpt: a full crawl must cover the entire confirmed scope before completing, because stale-document deletion removes anything absent from the run.

claims.text: Never let a partial fetch complete as a full crawl.
claims.excerpt: Never let a partial or failed fetch finish as a successful full crawl.

claims.text: Datasource name: ASCII letters and digits only.
claims.excerpt: CustomDatasourceConfig.name may contain only ASCII letters and digits

claims.text: Bulk indexing replaces the datasource; omitted documents are deleted.
claims.excerpt: Bulk indexing fully replaces the entire list of documents stored in Glean. After a successful bulk upload, all documents that were not a part of the most recent upload are deleted asynchronously.

claims.text: Timestamps are epoch seconds.
claims.excerpt: created_at and updated_at must be epoch seconds, not ISO strings.

claims.text: Intersection semantics.
claims.excerpt: A user must belong to every group within one entry; multiple entries are alternative intersections.

claims.text: Allow-all ACL defaults are the top review risk.
claims.excerpt: An allow-all default is the most consequential thing to miss.

claims.text: Groups require memberships.
claims.excerpt: If you return groups, you must also return memberships.

claims.text: extract_permission_refs() returns the user and group IDs the documents reference.
claims.excerpt: returning the deduplicated user_ids and group_ids your documents actually reference.

claims.text: The SDK does not persist checkpoints.
claims.excerpt: The SDK does not persist checkpoints

claims.text: Without an override, since is None and the data client falls back to a full fetch.
claims.excerpt: which means since is None and your data client falls back to a full fetch.

claims.text: max_items limits source consumption; it is not a Glean-side upload cap or a blast-radius guarantee.
claims.excerpt: max_items limits how many source items each registered client consumes. It is not a Glean-side upload cap or a blast-radius guarantee.

claims.text: --max-items is not a safety control.
claims.excerpt: Do not rely on --max-items to make a shared datasource safe

claims.text: An empty full crawl clears the datasource.
claims.excerpt: A successful empty full crawl sends one complete empty bulk page so all previously indexed documents are reconciled as stale.

claims.text: Checkpoint: start time, written only on success.
claims.excerpt: Record the timestamp from before the crawl started, and only write it after the run succeeds.

claims.text: force_restart only after a stuck upload.
claims.excerpt: Discards any in-progress upload session and starts a new one. Use after a crashed run leaves an upload stuck - not as a default.

claims.text: First and last pages are sequential.
claims.excerpt: the first opens the upload session, the last closes it and triggers stale deletion, so neither can race.

claims.text: index_documents() suits webhook updates.
claims.excerpt: This is the right call for event-driven connectors reacting to a webhook.

claims.text: Tune the dominant stage only.
claims.excerpt: Tuning upload concurrency when 90% of wall-clock is data_fetch accomplishes nothing.

claims.text: Prefer smaller batches over longer timeouts.
claims.excerpt: Smaller batches are usually the better answer.

claims.text: Each test phase swaps one dependency.
claims.excerpt: Each phase swaps exactly one thing from mocked to real, so a failure tells you which layer broke.

claims.text: Phase 2 rejects missing permissions, anonymous access, and all-datasource-users access because they prevent proving denial.
claims.excerpt: It also rejects missing permissions, allow_anonymous_access=True, and allow_all_datasource_users_access=True, because any of those prevents the harness from proving a configured identity is denied.

claims.text: Live tests need --allow-destructive-live.
claims.excerpt: Every live phase requires --allow-destructive-live

claims.text: Counts prove nothing about permissions.
claims.excerpt: Counting indexed documents proves nothing about permissions.

claims.text: Search as the user is ground truth.
claims.excerpt: the search result is the ground truth, not the upload response.

claims.text: Four-step missing-document diagnosis.
claims.excerpt: Most "the connector is broken" reports are really one of four things

claims.text: Accepted is not searchable.
claims.excerpt: Indexing is asynchronous - an accepted upload is not yet a searchable document.

claims.text: glean-idx datasource status shows uploaded and indexed counts, identity counts, visibility, and recent runs.
claims.excerpt: Uploaded and indexed counts per object type, identity counts, visibility, and the most recent upload and processing runs.

claims.text: glean-idx document access checks whether a given user can see a document.
claims.excerpt: Whether a given user can see a document

claims.text: ACLs fail without pushed identities.
claims.excerpt: a correct-looking ACL is still wrong if the identities it names were never pushed.

claims.text: teardown is irreversible.
claims.excerpt: teardown cannot be undone.

claims.text: CLI exit codes are stable.
claims.excerpt: SDK-owned exit codes are stable.

claims.text: Ambiguous writes are read back, not retried.
claims.excerpt: An ambiguous transport failure is reconciled by reading state back, never by blindly repeating the write.

claims.text: A connector is a batch job.
claims.excerpt: A connector is a batch job: it starts, pulls from a source, pushes to Glean, and exits.

claims.text: Observability is built in.
claims.excerpt: You get stage timings, item counts, and structured logs without adding any instrumentation.

claims.text: glean-idx deploy generates a Docker image and Terraform for a Kubernetes CronJob on GKE or EKS.
claims.excerpt: glean-idx deploy generates and operates a Docker image and Terraform for a Kubernetes CronJob on GKE or EKS.

claims.text: Connectors can run on many schedulers.
claims.excerpt: It can run as a VM cron job, Cloud Run or Lambda job, Airflow task, or scheduled CI workload.

claims.text: Alert on sharp drops in documents_indexed.
claims.excerpt: Alert on documents_indexed dropping sharply between runs

claims.text: Cloud telemetry plugins are mock-tested only.
claims.excerpt: The cloud provider plugins are currently tested only against mocks

claims.text: Full and incremental need separate configs.
claims.excerpt: A full and incremental schedule need separate deployment configurations

claims.text: A completed Job is not proof of indexing.
claims.excerpt: A completed Kubernetes Job proves only that the process exited successfully

claims.text: The Connector Builder explores the source API, plans with you, generates the connector against the SDK, and tests it before anything is indexed.
claims.excerpt: It explores the source's API, plans the connector with you, generates it against this SDK, and tests it before anything reaches your index.

claims.text: The Connector Builder runs mocked and recorded test phases before offering to index anything.
claims.excerpt: runs the mocked and recorded test phases before offering to index anything.

claims.text: Never allow-all 'for now'.
claims.excerpt: Never index sensitive content with an allow-all ACL "for now."

claims.text: Incremental needs a checkpoint and a deletion signal.
claims.excerpt: it needs a durable checkpoint and a reliable source-side deletion signal before it is correct rather than merely faster.
